## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Kilocode #13483: Cloud session import — CLI downloads cloud sessions locally (HIGH ~10h)

- **What**: Kilocode CLI can now download and continue existing cloud sessions locally. The `create_session` command accepts an optional `cloneFromKiloSessionId` string. When set, the CLI imports the cloud session in-process (fetches transcript, messages, parts from cloud API, persists locally, restores workspace files), attaches it, and defers workspace file restore + session-diff storage writes until after attach succeeds. Failed attach removes the imported session with no side effects. When absent, `create_session` starts a fresh session exactly as before. Cloud import logic moved from HTTP handler into a shared in-process helper (`importSession`, `importSessionWithoutRestore`, `finalizeSessionImport`) with four typed errors (unauthorized, upstream, bad-request, internal). Heartbeat capabilities object gains optional `sessionClone: true` flag so consumers can detect capable CLIs.
- **Why**: Users can start a session on web/desktop and continue it locally in CLI, or vice versa. Enables session mobility across client types without losing conversation history or workspace state.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13483 (feat(cli): import cloud transcript on create_session)
- **Category**: command (session management)
- **Size**: HIGH (~10h — Alexi has NO cloud session storage, NO `create_session` command, NO cloud API integration currently. Implementing cloud session import requires: (1) cloud session storage backend (S3/database for transcripts + messages), (2) cloud API endpoints (GET session, POST session, list sessions with auth), (3) CLI cloud auth (token/API key), (4) session import logic (fetch cloud transcript, persist locally to `~/.alexi/sessions/<id>.json`, restore workspace files if any, handle failures), (5) `sessions` CLI command extension to accept `--clone <cloud-session-id>` or similar flag, (6) heartbeat/capabilities protocol if Alexi adds multi-client session sharing. Pattern is CLI-portable but requires substantial infrastructure. Defer until cloud session persistence is prioritized).

#### 2. Cline #13587: Hub event memory leak — stop shipping full transcripts in broadcast events (MODERATE ~6h)

- **What**: Cline hub broadcast events (`session.updated`, `session.created`, `session.detached`, `run.started`) shipped the session's entire message transcript in every event's `snapshot.messages` field. Every status flip re-read all messages from disk just to emit a state event, put the whole conversation on the wire per subscriber, into the durable event log, and into websocket send queues. A subscriber draining slower than events arrive made the hub retain one full-transcript copy per event, causing multi-GB memory leaks (reported 25GB hub process on 16GB Mac with 7.5MB sessions = ~3,700 retained transcript copies). Repro: stub hub + slow consumer hit 5.3GB `bufferedAmount` in 40s, heapUsed tracking 1:1. Fix: strip `snapshot.messages` from all broadcast events and replies — snapshots are state notifications (status, usage, model, workspace, capabilities, checkpoint), not transcript carriers. Audit confirmed no consumer reads `snapshot.messages` from events/replies (desktop sidecar reads only `session.status`, `HubRuntimeHost` uses `artifacts.messagesPath`/usage/status, VS Code treats events as list-refresh triggers). Transcript fetched separately via `session.messages` command. Checkpoint-restore snapshots (session-versioning-service) unchanged — restore replies carry messages in dedicated `messages` field (user-initiated request-scoped operation, not broadcast). Side benefit: `emitStatus` no longer does full-transcript disk read + JSON clone per status change.
- **Why**: Defensive coding — broadcast state events should never embed unbounded user content (transcripts can be multi-MB). Prevents memory leaks when slow subscribers accumulate send-queue backlog.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13587 (fix(hub): stop shipping full transcripts inside broadcast hub events)
- **Category**: tool (infrastructure/memory)
- **Size**: MODERATE (~6h — Alexi has NO hub daemon mode, NO multi-client session sharing, NO broadcast events currently. SessionManager (src/core/sessionManager.ts L1-726) persists sessions to `~/.alexi/sessions/` as JSON files, read/write is synchronous per-command, no event bus or broadcast subscription. Pattern is CLI-portable if/when Alexi adds multi-client session sharing (e.g. TUI + headless CLI sharing one session, or web UI + CLI). General principle: session state snapshots (status, usage, model, workdir) should NEVER embed the full transcript — transcript is fetched on-demand via separate query. If Alexi adds session event broadcasting, apply this pattern from day one).

#### 3. Cline #13512: Apply_patch CRLF preservation — preserve file's own line endings across patch updates (MODERATE ~5h)

- **What**: Cline's `apply_patch` tool normalized originals to LF so parser and chunk math could match the model's LF-only patch text, but forgot to restore the file's original EOL on write. A one-line patch to a CRLF file silently converted the whole file to LF, producing huge every-line diffs on Windows, destroying `git blame`, and leaving mixed-EOL repos. Impact: ~500k `apply_patch` calls by ~7.5k Windows users in 14 days. Fix: `loadFiles` records each file's detected EOL alongside LF-normalized content, chunk math runs in LF space (unchanged), `patchToChanges` restores the file's own EOL to `oldContent`/`newContent` on the way out. UPDATE (including moves) writes the file back in its original endings. ADD keeps platform-native normalization from #13521. `detectLineEnding`/`normalizeLineEndings` moved from `editor.ts` into shared `line-endings.ts` so both executors use one implementation. Mixed-EOL files come out uniformly in detected EOL (CRLF if any `\r\n` present).
- **Why**: Cross-platform correctness — patching a CRLF file should preserve CRLF, not silently rewrite to LF and trigger whole-file diffs.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13512 (fix(tools): preserve a file's own CRLF line endings across apply_patch updates)
- **Category**: tool (apply_patch)
- **Size**: MODERATE (~5h — Alexi src/tool/tools/apply-patch.ts L1-307 already handles encoding via `detectEncoding(buffer)` L242, `decodeWithEncoding(buffer, encoding)` L245, `encodeWithEncoding(patchedContent, encoding)` L261, but has NO line-ending detection or restoration. `applyPatchToContent` L63-173 splits on `\n` L68 but does not record original EOL, so a CRLF file patched by Alexi would be rewritten to LF (same bug as Cline pre-#13512). Implement: (1) `detectLineEnding(content: string): 'CRLF' | 'LF'` (scan for `\r\n`, return `'CRLF'` if found else `'LF'`), (2) normalize originalContent to LF before applyPatchToContent L248, (3) restore detected EOL after patching by replacing `\n` with `\r\n` if original was CRLF, (4) write restored content L261. Reuse eol-normalizer.ts L1-66 helpers if possible, or implement minimal inline logic).

#### 4. Kilocode #13512: Worktree references — searchable worktree picker for VS Code agent-manager (LOW/SKIP)

- **What**: Kilocode VS Code agent-manager adds a **Worktrees** entry to the `@` menu. Opens a searchable picker (shared `List` component, same row styling as Past chats). Selection inserts the absolute worktree path and attaches a small text record (branch, base branch, session IDs/titles). Does NOT attach directory contents, diffs, or conversation history, does NOT change agent's working directory or bypass tool permissions. Reuses active project's worktree inventory and session projection, no new backend endpoint. Sorting: recent worktree visits first (bounded to 100 paths in webview state), then latest activity (worktree creation or session update), then sidebar order. Typed query uses shared List's fuzzy ranking over names/branches/session titles. Current worktree, missing worktrees, and worktrees undergoing operations are excluded.
- **Why**: Comparing work across agent-manager worktrees currently requires copying directory paths or attaching past conversations when only a reference is needed.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13512 (feat(vscode): add searchable worktree references)
- **Category**: tool (UI/references)
- **Size**: LOW (Kilocode VS Code agent-manager feature — desktop GUI with webview picker, worktree inventory state, recency tracking, `@` menu integration, searchable List component. Alexi is CLI-only with NO desktop GUI, NO agent-manager, NO worktree management, NO `@` menu (TUI has no webview). Pattern is not CLI-portable, SKIP).

#### 6. Cline #13612: Scheduled task final output — auto-expand submit_and_exit and render summary as markdown (LOW/SKIP)

- **What**: Cline desktop app scheduled tasks (routines) run in yolo mode with required completion tool `submit_and_exit({ summary, verified })`. That summary is the run's final deliverable, but chat transcript rendered it as a generic tool row (collapsed by default, monospace code block when expanded). Fix: `submit_and_exit` row auto-expands as soon as summary text is available (users can still collapse manually), summary renders through app's markdown pipeline (Streamdown with safe links/images) instead of `ToolActivityCode` block (headings/lists/emphasis display properly), summary renders in full foreground color instead of muted gray (it is primary output user reads). Added `extractSubmitSummaryText` to desktop tool-summary layer (prefers input's `summary` field, falls back to extracted result text echoed by scheduled-run executor). No changes to shared `@cline/ui` tool-summary or SDK, purely desktop transcript presentation.
- **Why**: Scheduled task final summaries are the run's deliverable — should be readable at a glance, not buried in a collapsed tool panel.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13612 (Desktop: surface scheduled-task final output — auto-expand submit_and_exit and render its summary as markdown)
- **Category**: cli (UI/output)
- **Size**: LOW (Cline desktop app transcript rendering — Tauri GUI with React/Streamdown markdown renderer, tool row auto-expand state, `ToolActivityCode` vs markdown panel toggling, `submit_and_exit` tool semantic awareness. Alexi is CLI-only with NO desktop app, NO scheduled tasks/routines, NO `submit_and_exit` tool, NO transcript panel UI. TUI (src/cli/tui/) uses Ink + marked + marked-terminal for markdown rendering, but has NO tool row collapsing or `submit_and_exit` completion semantics. Pattern only relevant if Alexi adds scheduled autonomous tasks with completion summaries — then surface summary prominently in TUI output. SKIP for now).

#### 7. Cline #13218: ProtoBus tunneling over Host Bridge — gRPC bidirectional stream for IntelliJ reverse calls (LOW/SKIP)

- **What**: Cline standalone cores (IntelliJ plugin backend) previously opened a second gRPC listener so IntelliJ could call back into the core. Listener port chosen before spawning Node, causing TOCTOU probe/bind window. Fix: carry reverse ProtoBus requests over authenticated bidirectional stream on existing Host Bridge connection instead. Core removes per-spawn token before child processes inherit it, reports readiness only after local init completes, preserves TCP listener only for standalone CLI harness (starts without token). Protocol carries generated service/method identities, unary/streaming responses, structured errors, cancellation. Generated metadata is source of truth for streaming mode. Companion integration: cline/intellij-plugin#1110.
- **Why**: IntelliJ plugin needs reverse calls into core (e.g. tool execution callbacks), but second listener has TOCTOU race and doubles port allocation.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13218 (Tunnel ProtoBus over the existing Host Bridge)
- **Category**: tool (infrastructure/gRPC)
- **Size**: LOW (Cline IntelliJ plugin integration — gRPC bidirectional stream, Host Bridge protocol extension, standalone core spawn token lifecycle, reverse call routing. Alexi is CLI-only with NO IntelliJ plugin, NO gRPC Host Bridge, NO standalone core spawn model. Pattern not CLI-portable, SKIP).
